clue.text: Decorate popular curry place to get new look?

parts.note: to dress a shop window or a tree is to decorate it
in, as in 'the in thing', means fashionable or popular
to curry a horse is to groom it with a comb

explanation.surface: Someone plans to spruce up a favourite Indian restaurant to give it a fresh image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curry' looks like food but is the verb for brushing a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors and shoppers change clothes and make-up in such a room, emerging with an altered appearance.

clue.text: Melody making cast end in chaos?

indicators.note: letters in chaos are thrown into disorder, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tune that sends a play's cast into disarray at the finish.
explanation.definitionFit: A descant is a counter-melody sung above the main tune, as in carols.

clue.text: Offer a service collecting excise

indicators.note: the phrase collects, or holds within it, the letters of the answer

explanation.surface: An offer of service that includes a tax charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excise' reads as a tax, but here it is the verb meaning cut out.
explanation.definitionFit: To excise is to cut something out or remove it, the same as wiping it away.

clue.text: Plant rush successfully

parts.note: to rush is to speed along
doing something well is doing it successfully

explanation.surface: Instructions to grow a plant quickly and with good results.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedwell is a small flowering plant of the Veronica genus, usually blue.

clue.text: A right to be in US city? Never!

indicators.note: the letters for 'a right' are placed inside the city abbreviation

parts.note: NY is short for New York

explanation.surface: Someone flatly refuses the idea of a right being granted in an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Nary is a dialect word meaning not one, used as an emphatic never.

clue.text: Capital Italian island with a new following from another country?

indicators.note: the letters for 'a new' follow on after the earlier pieces

parts.note: a Roman is an Italian from the capital, Rome

explanation.surface: A Roman visits an island with a fresh band of admirers drawn from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer is one specific nationality, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A Romanian comes from Romania, a foreign country from the viewpoint of a British solver.

clue.text: Cop worried about note one found behind bars

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go about, or around, the note and the one
something worried is disturbed, so the letters of cop are jumbled

parts.note: T (te) is a note of the sol-fa scale
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A police officer frets over a message from someone in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worried' turns COP into OPC, and 'about' wraps that round TI.
explanation.definitionFit: An optic is the measuring device fitted to upturned spirit bottles behind a pub bar.

clue.text: Attractive engraving with female head

indicators.note: the letter for female goes at the head, in front of the rest

parts.note: an etching is a print made from an engraved plate

explanation.surface: A lovely print showing a woman's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Fetching describes someone or something charming and good-looking.

clue.text: Stick diamonds in a present!

indicators.note: the diamonds letter is placed in the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: to be here is to be present
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A suggestion to fix jewels into a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to stick fast to a surface or a cause.

clue.text: Sandown empty and a Grand National winner that gets beaten!

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its insides, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: Red Rum won the Grand National, Britain's great steeplechase, three times in the 1970s

explanation.surface: A racing scene at Sandown Park with no crowd and a famous champion horse who gets beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandown is an English racecourse; 'beaten' suggests a lost race but means struck.
explanation.definitionFit: A snare drum is a percussion instrument, struck with sticks to make it sound.

clue.text: Pace of study after tea being delivered

indicators.note: study comes after the tea piece
a word delivered in speech is spoken, so tea becomes the letter it is pronounced as

parts.note: the drink is said exactly like the letter T
to read a subject at university is to study it

explanation.surface: Someone's speed of work after their cuppa has arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: A tread is a step or the sound of footfall, so it can mean one's walking pace.

clue.text: Changes the last word — 'dust', oddly

parts.note: amen is said at the very end of a prayer

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters, first and third, are taken

explanation.surface: A funeral rite: 'ashes to ashes, dust' revised at the final word.
explanation.definitionFit: Amends as a verb means alters or corrects, as with a document.

clue.text: Relation may garage freezing cold vehicle for one

indicators.note: garaging something puts it inside, so the relation holds the other piece

parts.note: an uncle is a family relation
icy means freezing cold

explanation.surface: A relative might keep a cold vehicle in their garage.
explanation.definitionFit: A unicycle has a single wheel and carries only its rider.

clue.text: Canopy of trees disturbed by what, ultimately?

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word
the letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone notices the treetops shaken and wonders by what.
explanation.definitionFit: A tester is an old word for a canopy over a four-poster bed or pulpit.

clue.text: Stand still, seeing a gun unloaded in Texas, perhaps

indicators.note: the middle pieces go inside the word for Texas

parts.note: Texas is an example of a US state

indicators.note: a gun unloaded loses its centre, leaving only the outside letters

explanation.surface: A Texan freezes on seeing an empty firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagnate is to stop moving or developing, like still water.

clue.text: Plant a parliamentarian in county

indicators.note: the pieces are placed inside the county word

parts.note: shire is an old word for a county
MP stands for Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An instruction to install a politician in a provincial seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a verb meaning install, but it is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Samphire is a coastal plant with fleshy edible shoots.

clue.text: Corral beast grabbing Republican correspondent

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure like a corral

indicators.note: the outer pieces grab hold of the party letter

parts.note: a fiend is a monster or beast

explanation.surface: A cowboy rounds up a monster that has seized a politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen pal is someone who exchanges letters, a regular correspondent.

clue.text: This might hold lace worked under canvas structure

indicators.note: in a down answer the rearranged lace sits below the tent

parts.note: a tent is made of canvas

indicators.note: worked letters are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: Lacework being done beneath a marquee.
explanation.definitionFit: An octopus grips things with its long flexible arms, which exist to grasp.

clue.text: Fools rest, covered in burns

indicators.note: the rest piece is covered inside the burns word

parts.note: chars means scorches or burns
to lie is to rest

explanation.surface: An injured person lies down, covered in burns.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlie is British slang for a silly person, as in 'a right charlie'.

clue.text: Farm stock let out by lion?

parts.note: a lion is a big cat

indicators.note: out signals the letters of let are put out of order

explanation.surface: Livestock released by a lion on the loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Cows and oxen kept on a farm are livestock.

clue.text: Starting late, imagine tricky puzzle

indicators.note: tricky suggests the remaining letters are twisted into a new order
starting late means the word misses its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone imagines a hard puzzle after a slow start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starting late' drops the I of imagine, leaving MAGINE, which 'tricky' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a mystery or riddle that is hard to solve.

clue.text: Cause of reaction that's largely violent

indicators.note: violent upheaval throws these letters about

explanation.surface: Something behind a reaction that is mostly violent.
explanation.definitionFit: An allergy is a sensitivity that makes the body react to pollen, nuts and so on.

clue.text: Determination shown by 'X', a population centre

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten
a city is a centre of population

explanation.surface: Grit displayed by an unnamed big town marked X.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenacity is persistence, refusing to let go of a goal.

clue.text: How one might come for confession?

definitions.text: How one might come for confession?

parts.words: How one might come for confession?
parts.note: to come ... is to own up, and a penitent arriving at confession may also be freshly washed

explanation.surface: A question about how to present oneself at church to confess.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming clean is an idiom for admitting the truth, as in a confession.

clue.text: Unpleasant experience of gold trade

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
a deal is a trade or transaction

explanation.surface: A miserable time spent dealing in bullion.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a painful or trying experience.

clue.text: Surplus old paintings put up

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: in a down answer, putting up reads the word upward, backwards

parts.note: art means paintings collectively

explanation.surface: Spare antique pictures hung on the wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional, beyond what is needed.

clue.text: Humans' earliest form of transport?

parts.note: not ancient history but each person's first ride, as a baby pushed around

explanation.surface: A question seemingly about the dawn of travel in human history.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue suggests the wheel or a raft; it means the first vehicle in each life.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby carriage is the first vehicle most infants ride in.

clue.text: Coffee — the second of two unfinished

indicators.note: unfinished means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: the latter is the second of two things mentioned

explanation.surface: Of two coffees, the second was left undrunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A latte is an espresso drink made with lots of steamed milk.

clue.text: One plying craft made of log going after fish

parts.note: a carp is a freshwater fish
to log something is to enter it in a record

explanation.surface: Someone sails a boat built from a tree trunk in pursuit of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' and 'log' suggest boats; the craft is woodworking and 'going after' just sets the order.
explanation.definitionFit: A joiner or woodworker practises a trade, or craft, with timber.

clue.text: Factor in school session with European journal

parts.note: a term is a period of the school year
a diary is a daily journal

explanation.surface: Something in a school term involving a European diary.
explanation.definitionFit: A factor in the old sense is an agent who acts on another's behalf, a go-between.
